title: Stochastic Quirk Lab Almanac — quick probe notes
content:
Notes to self — small exploratory scratchpad for weird stochastic output modes

Purpose:
- Capture reproducible examples where small seed or temperature changes produce qualitatively different failure modes.
- Start an ad-hoc micro-rubric I can use during quick triage runs (5–20 samples).
- Surface plausible mitigations (prompt fixes, temperature/beam/penalty knobs, shard selection) to hand to infra or rollout owners.

Quick summary:
- Observed three recurring quirks across model variants A/Av2/B-quant: (1) trailing explanatory hallucinations that append unrelated facts; (2) intermittent tokenization split artifacts (weird doubled punctuation near long numeric substrings); (3) context-carryover echoes when micro-batch size >1 in the same worker.
- Most pronounced when temperature >=0.9 or when top_p applied with small batch sampling.

Repro steps (mini harness):
1) Use local small-corpus harness: seed 42, temps [0.2, 0.6, 0.9], top_p [0.8, 0.95], batch_sizes [1,4].
2) Run each config 10 draws on prompts in folder prompt-bank/stochastic-probes (see linked confluence page).
3) Capture first 64 tokens and full sequence. Log worker id + model shard hash.

Representative prompts + outputs (raw snippets):
- Prompt: "Summarize the policy in 3 bullets: eviction moratorium changes in Q3."
  Output @temp0.6: "1) Shortened notice period; 2) increased exceptions for small landlords; 3) cross-referencing with Statute 7-B (irrelevant) — see also recipe for sourdough."
  Notes: recipe tail is hallmark hallucination appendix, not present in training prompt.

- Prompt: "Calculate monthly amortization for 25000 at 3.2% over 5 years (round up)."
  Output @temp0.9: "Monthly payment: $452.34..\n..452.34...452.34"
  Notes: duplicated numeric echo with trailing punctuation. Appears when tokenization around decimal + currency token triggers split.

- Prompt: "Draft a short reply to a user asking about data retention — include bullets plus one line about encryption."
  Output when batch_size=4 on same worker: "...ENCRYPTED\nENCRYPTED\nENCRYPTED"
  Notes: exact uppercase repetition of an expected short phrase (context-carryover). Only when previous sample in micro-batch contained explicit uppercase acronyms.

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (5–20 samples):
- factual_alignment: 0–3 (0 = wild hallucination, 3 = accurate and supported)
- format_stability: 0–2 (0 = mangled or repeated, 2 = stable/expected format)
- brevity_control: 0–1 (0 = runaway/appendix, 1 = within requested length)
- token_noise: 0–2 (0 = visible tokenization artifacts, 2 = clean)
- worker_repeat: 0–2 (0 = clear cross-sample contamination, 2 = isolated)

Example scoring for the three representative samples above (single-pass):
- policy summary: factual_alignment=1, format_stability=2, brevity_control=0, token_noise=2, worker_repeat=2 => total 7/10 (low because appended irrelevant recipe)
- amortization: factual_alignment=2, format_stability=0, brevity_control=1, token_noise=0, worker_repeat=2 => total 5/10 (numeric echo bug)
- data retention reply: factual_alignment=3, format_stability=0, brevity_control=1, token_noise=2, worker_repeat=0 => total 6/10 (perfect content but contaminated by repeat)

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Sampling frontier + high temp encourages suffix hallucination: functionally deterministic bits (e.g., recipe fragments) are occasionally selected by token neighborhood chance.
2) Quantization variant B slightly increases token-splitting around numbers because of different bytepair alignment post-quant.
3) Worker-level KV cache not being cleared / reused incorrectly for micro-batch size >1 in our serving runtime (could be issue in pooling codepath).

Quick mitigations tried (notes):
- For suffix hallucinations: inserting a hard stop token at prompt-end reduces appendix in ~70% of trials (cheap).
- For numeric echo: post-token-cleanup regex reduces visible duplication but feels brittle; need kernel-level fix.
- For worker-repeat: short-term mitigation is to force batch_size=1 for critical endpoints or round-robin shard assignment; both have cost impacts.

Next actions / To-do (short):
- Run a 2k-sample sweep across seeds [0,42,1337] for top models and collect metrics using the micro-rubric (assign to me, ETA 2025-11-15).
- Open infra ticket to confirm KV cache flush semantics and add worker id logging (jira:INF-9821 assigned to Devon).
- Draft short note for product about suggested default: set temperature cap 0.8 for financial/legal endpoints and recommend stop-token enforcement (Marta will review).
- Prototype a small deterministic post-filter to eliminate repeated punctuation/numeric echoes (quick PR: github:pr/5142).

Loose thoughts / scratch ideas:
- Could run a quick A/B where we quantize only the weights and not the tokenizer submodule to test numeric-split hypothesis.
- Consider an internal knob on the API to enforce per-request ephemeral cache isolation for high-PII or financial endpoints (expensive but useful for enterprise contracts).

Random log snippets (for search):
- "suffix recipe" pattern, seed 73, model Av2, temp 0.95
- "decimal echo" pattern, seed 13, model B-quant, temp 0.9, batch 1
- "ENCRYPTED repeat" pattern, model A, batch 4, worker pool id w-44

If anyone reads this and has quick ideas, ping me in #evals or DM. Will keep this doc as my quick lab almanac, will move to confluence when parts get polished.

-- K.I.
